items.headline: Singapore graduates take traineeships at half the median starting pay as hiring cools
items.summary: Unemployed fresh graduates are turning to government-funded Graduate Industry Traineeships paying S$1,800-S$2,400 a month, less than half the median graduate starting salary, as firms stay cautious.

items.headline: Singapore-flagged cargo ship struck by a projectile while crossing the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: A Singapore-flagged vessel operated by Taiwan's Evergreen Marine was hit by an unidentified projectile near Oman; the UN subsequently paused its escort of ships through the strait.

items.headline: Analysts say Wong-Putin meeting does not signal Singapore softening on Russia
items.summary: Observers framed PM Lawrence Wong's meeting with Vladimir Putin, held as part of an ASEAN delegation, as pragmatic diplomacy that keeps channels open while leaving sanctions on Moscow intact.

items.headline: New speed camera on the BKE near Woodlands goes live on 1 July
items.summary: Traffic Police announced a new speed-detection camera at the 9km mark of the Bukit Timah Expressway towards Woodlands, operational from 1 July; speeding cases rose from 201,358 in 2024 to 253,550 in 2025.

items.headline: Banks pledge an ATM or cashpoint within 500m of every HDB block by end-2027
items.summary: DBS, OCBC, UOB and NETS committed to placing an ATM, branch or cashpoint within 500m of every HDB block by end-2027, among 20 new initiatives from the Association of Banks in Singapore.

items.headline: George Kurian resigns ahead of an expected Modi cabinet reshuffle this weekend
items.summary: Union Minister of State George Kurian resigned on 23 June as a Union Cabinet reshuffle is widely reported as imminent around 28-29 June; portfolio changes for several ministers are being speculated, with no official announcement made.

items.headline: S&P pegs India's FY27 growth at 6.6% as a weak monsoon clouds the outlook
items.summary: S&P Global Ratings projected India's GDP growth at 6.6% for FY27, flagging energy stress, a weak monsoon, inflation and global uncertainty.

items.headline: GSTN flags e-invoice and e-way bill API changes; flood-hit Maharashtra gets filing relief
items.summary: The GST Network issued an advisory on changes to e-invoice and e-Way Bill APIs effective 1 August; the CBIC extended GST filing deadlines for several heavy-rain-hit Maharashtra districts.

items.headline: Burnham becomes front-runner for Labour leadership after Starmer's resignation
items.summary: Keir Starmer resigned as PM and Labour leader on 22 June; Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham, newly elected MP for Makerfield with a majority above 9,200, leads the field after Wes Streeting ruled himself out; nominations open 9 July.

items.headline: Resident doctors' ballot on a 6.6% pay offer closes; result will decide the strikes
items.summary: England's resident doctors voted on the government's offer of an average 6.6% pay uplift by April 2027 plus pay-structure reform, in a ballot that closed at noon on 26 June.

items.headline: OBR puts UK welfare spending at 314.9bn pounds, or 10.7% of GDP
items.summary: The OBR's June Welfare Trends Report put UK welfare spending at 314.9bn pounds (10.7% of GDP) in 2024/25, forecast to rise to 333.7bn in 2025/26 and 408.6bn by 2030/31.

items.headline: Update: Venezuela quake toll passes 1,400 as the 72-hour rescue window closes
items.summary: The death toll from Wednesday's twin earthquakes near Caracas climbed past 1,400 with more than 4,500 injured; around 1,600 foreign rescuers joined the search as the 72-hour window expired.

items.headline: Update: US strikes Iran for a second night after a tanker is hit near Hormuz
items.summary: US Central Command struck Iranian missile, drone and radar sites for a second consecutive night after a drone hit the tanker M/T Kiku, threatening the 17 June US-Iran memorandum.

items.headline: Germany sets an all-time heat record of 41.5C as Europe's heatwave shifts east
items.summary: Germany recorded a national high of 41.5C at Drewitz as an extreme heatwave linked to dozens of deaths pushed into Germany and Poland, disrupting rail, power and events.

items.headline: Aid groups warn of imminent atrocities as the RSF encircles Sudan's el-Obeid
items.summary: Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch and others urged action to avert mass killings in el-Obeid, besieged by the RSF for some 18 months, with the UN saying 500,000 civilians are at risk.

items.headline: Tropical Storm Mekkhala floods Taiwan, killing two before heading for Japan
items.summary: Outer bands of Tropical Storm Mekkhala triggered severe flooding across Taiwan, killing two and closing offices and schools for over five million residents, before moving toward Japan where 2.2 million were told to evacuate.

items.headline: US clears Anthropic's Mythos 5 model for about 100 trusted partners
items.summary: The Commerce Department granted Anthropic permission to release its Mythos 5 model to roughly 100 companies and federal agencies; restrictions on the related Fable 5 model were left unchanged.

items.headline: Asian AI labs rush out rival models as the US export curbs drag on
items.summary: China's 360 unveiled Tulongfeng, pitched as a Mythos rival, and Tokyo-based Sakana AI launched Fugu, which it says stands shoulder-to-shoulder with leading Western frontier models.

items.headline: Despite the AI hype, engineering is the most resilient tech job, new data shows
items.summary: SignalFire's State of Talent Report found engineering was the most resilient tech function in 2025: total big-tech hiring fell 25% versus 2019 but engineering roles dropped just 11%.

items.headline: Cybersecurity startup NewCore raises $66m to give AI agents identities
items.summary: NewCore emerged from stealth with $66m led by Cyberstarts, valuing it at $300m, to build identity and access tooling for autonomous AI agents.

items.headline: Equal-weight S&P 500 hits a record as the rally broadens away from chipmakers
items.summary: Investors rotated out of chipmakers into broader growth names, leaving the cap-weighted S&P 500 little changed on Friday while its equal-weighted version reached record highs.

items.headline: Caterpillar jumps about 6% as industrials carry the Dow to a record
items.summary: Caterpillar surged roughly 6% as industrials lifted the Dow to a fresh intraday high; investors treat it as an AI-infrastructure play, with Q1 sales up 22% to $17.4bn.

items.headline: Silver slides below $65 an ounce as the Fed flags a possible rate hike
items.summary: Silver corrected sharply to about $65, down roughly 46% from its January peak, as a stronger dollar and rising yields hit precious metals and the Fed signalled possible hikes.

items.headline: Nasdaq logs a fifth straight loss as money rotates into defensives
items.summary: The Nasdaq closed at 25,297.62 for a fifth consecutive losing session; for the week the S&P 500 slid nearly 2% and the Nasdaq fell 4.6% as investors moved into defensives.

items.headline: 🏎️ Russell takes a dramatic Austrian GP pole as Verstappen crashes out in Q3
items.summary: George Russell clocked 1:06.113 to beat Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton to pole in Saturday's qualifying at the Red Bull Ring after Max Verstappen crashed in Q3; Antonelli starts fourth, Verstappen fifth.

items.headline: 🏎️ Mercedes sweep Austrian practice as Russell pips Antonelli in final practice
items.summary: George Russell topped final practice at the Red Bull Ring with a 1:07.096, edging Kimi Antonelli by 0.038s to complete a Mercedes sweep of all three sessions before qualifying.

items.headline: 🎾 Muchova wins her first grass title at Bad Homburg as Osaka retires in the final
items.summary: Karolina Muchova claimed her maiden grass-court title after Naomi Osaka retired with a foot injury trailing 6-1, 1-0, raising fitness questions days before Wimbledon.

items.headline: 🎾 Keys becomes a three-time Eastbourne champion without dropping a set
items.summary: Madison Keys beat Tatjana Maria 7-5, 6-4 in the Eastbourne final to lift the trophy a third time, joining Chris Evert and Martina Navratilova as the only three-time women's champions.

items.headline: 🏏 England rout New Zealand by nine wickets to knock out the holders
items.summary: England finished their Women's T20 World Cup group unbeaten with a nine-wicket win over New Zealand; Danni Wyatt-Hodge (89*) and Sophia Dunkley (49*) chased 164 to eliminate the holders.

items.headline: 🏏 West Indies reach the T20 World Cup semis despite Ireland's first-ever win
items.summary: West Indies advanced to the Women's T20 World Cup semi-finals even after losing to Ireland by six wickets in Bristol, Ireland's first World Cup victory behind Orla Prendergast's fifty.

items.headline: NASA prepares the first robotic rescue of a falling space telescope
items.summary: NASA's ~$30m Swift Boost mission will use a commercial robot called LINK to grapple the engineless 22-year-old Swift observatory and boost it to a higher orbit, the first capture of a satellite never designed to be serviced.

items.headline: Euclid maps the Milky Way's crowded heart, imaging more than 60 million stars
items.summary: ESA's Euclid telescope released an intermediate Galactic Bulge Survey, imaging nine fields across 4.8 square degrees and over 60 million stars to help find and weigh exoplanets via microlensing.

items.headline: Adaptive deep brain stimulation cuts falls for Parkinson's patients in a trial
items.summary: A Nature Medicine study found gait-synchronized adaptive deep brain stimulation is feasible and safe and reduces falls versus continuous stimulation, using personalized gait-phase biomarkers in five patients.

items.headline: NASA's Roman Space Telescope arrives in Florida for final launch preparations
items.summary: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope arrived at Kennedy Space Center for final prelaunch work ahead of a 2026 liftoff; it will survey wide swathes of sky to probe dark energy and hunt exoplanets.

fun_fact.headline: The world's shortest scheduled commercial flight, Westray to Papa Westray, lasts under two minutes.
fun_fact.body: The world's shortest scheduled commercial flight connects the Scottish islands of Westray and Papa Westray and lasts under two minutes (about 90 seconds with a fair wind). Operated by Loganair, it is recognised by Guinness World Records.

puzzle.title: Hidden Rectangles
puzzle.body: In a 4x4 grid of small squares, how many rectangles of any size lie along the grid lines (including the small squares and the whole square)?
puzzle.approach: Count the grid lines, then the ways to choose two of them in each direction.
puzzle.answer: 100 rectangles: C(5,2) x C(5,2) = 10 x 10 = 100 (of which 30 are squares).

word_puzzle.title: From Head to Tail
word_puzzle.body: Turn HEAD into TAIL, changing one letter at a time, each step a valid four-letter word, in five steps.
word_puzzle.approach: Change one letter at a time; every rung must be a real word.
word_puzzle.answer: HEAD -> HEAL -> TEAL -> TELL -> TALL -> TAIL
